chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! A performer of Tamattu' visits the House (the Kaaba), so he performs the Tawaf of Hajj, then he performs the Tawaf of the Women (Nisa), then he performs Sa'ee.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Sa'ee does not occur except before the Tawaf of the Women.' So I said: 'Is there anything upon him (a penalty)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Sa'ee does not occur except before the Tawaf of the Women.'

key_terms.سَعَى: He performed Sa'ee (the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf of the Women, a specific Tawaf performed by the Mu'tamir after returning from Mina/Arafat before Sa'ee
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْحَجِّ: The Tawaf of Hajj (Tawaf al-Qudum or Tawaf al-Ziyarah depending on context, here likely referring to the initial Tawaf)
key_terms.طَوَافِ النِّسَاءِ: The Tawaf of the Women (genitive case)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, known as Tamattu'

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of Sa'ee and Tawaf al-Nisa for a Mu'tamir in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the ritual sequence for a Mu'tamir, emphasizing that Sa'ee must precede Tawaf al-Nisa to be valid for Hajj. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of Tawaf al-Nisa as a separate obligation rather than an integral part of the primary Tawaf, a view central to Shia jurisprudence. The repetition of the Imam's statement underscores the importance of correct order in completing the pillars of Hajj.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! A performer of Tumatto visits the House (Kabah), so he performs a Tawaaf, being the Tawaaf of the Hajj. Then he performs a Tawaaf, being Tawaaf of the women (طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ). Then he performs Sa’ee’. So heasws said: ‘The Sa’ee does not happen to be except before the Tawaaf of the women (طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ)’. So I said, ‘Is there anything upon him?’ So heasws said: ‘The Sa’ee does not happen to be except before the Tawaaf of the women (طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man for al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous), saying , ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, if he can visit the House, perform Tawaf of al-Hajj, then Tawaf al-Nisa’, then Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah. He (the Imam) said, ‘Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah is not obligatory except before Tawaf al-Nisa V I then asked, ’Does he owe anything upon him because of this?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al- Marwah is not obligatory except before Tawaf al-Nisa V”
